terms.grammar: adjective, third declension; answered by quālis
evidence: Phaedr. 3.9.6: tam angustam tālis vir pōnis domum?
Sen. Ep. 75.1: quālis sermō meus esset … tālēs esse epistulās meās volō
terms.comment: Of kind. Its pair is quālis: tālis … quālis, such … as.

evidence: Verg. A. 2.594: quis indomitās tantus dolor excitat īrās?
terms.comment: Of size and amount: tantus … quantus, as great … as.

terms.grammar: adverb, before an adjective or adverb
terms.comment: English “such a small house” is tam angusta domus, “so small a house”.

terms.gloss: of that (this) kind, that sort of
terms.grammar: genitive of quality, after its noun
evidence: Cic. Fin. 5.48: pompā, lūdīs atque ejus modī spectāculīs

phrases.latin: quaesō, tam angustam tālis vir pōnis domum? — utinam, inquit, vērīs hanc amīcīs impleam!
phrases.english: Tell me, does a man like you build himself so small a house? — I only wish, he said, I could fill it with true friends!

phrases.latin: ō suāvis anima! quāle tē dīcam bonum antehāc fuisse, tālēs cum sint reliquiae?
phrases.english: O sweet breath! How good must you have been before, when your dregs are such as these?

phrases.latin: quālis sermō meus esset sī ūnā dēsidērēmus aut ambulārēmus, inlabōrātus et facilis, tālēs esse epistulās meās volō
phrases.english: I want my letters to be such as my talk would be if we were sitting or walking together: unlaboured and easy

phrases.latin: nāte, quis indomitās tantus dolor excitat īrās? quid furis?
phrases.english: My son, what pain so great stirs up such wild anger? Why are you raging?
